examples.text: We prefer local produce.

glosses: Connected directly to a particular computer, processor, etc.; able to be accessed offline.

local file

glosses: Having limited scope (either lexical or dynamic); only accessible within a certain portion of a program.
Applying to or satisfied by substructures understood as \"near points;\" in particular:
Satisfied by at least one open neighborhood of every point.

examples.text: A Hausdorff space satisfying local compactness need not be (globally) compact!

Such that the following conditions are equivalent: (1) P holds for R (M); (2) P holds for the localization R_p (M_p) for all prime ideals p of R; (3) P holds for the localization R_m (M_m) for all maximal ideals m of R.

examples.text: Flatness is a local property.

glosses: A person who lives in or near a given place.

examples.text: It's easy to tell the locals from the tourists.

glosses: A locally scoped identifier.

examples.text: Functional programming languages usually don't allow changing the immediate value of locals once they've been initialized, unless they're explicitly marked as being mutable.
